_meta.provenance: v2: the three limits frames below are byte-exact captures (hex copied from findings-update, taken from fixtures.txt). They were decoded again by an independent decoder on 2026-10-14: every Connect length adds up (5 + 119 = 124 bytes), doubles 0.76 and 0.25 and the epoch values recompute exactly. Field numbers and meanings are still inferred from values, there is no schema (API is v1alpha). Frames marked synthetic or reconstructed are NOT captures.
_meta.frame_hex_note: limits frames: byte-exact. keepalive, end_cadence: structurally exact, built from the known bytes/JSON. text_delta_emoji: synthetic block id, real structure. Other frames are decoded form only.
_meta.privacy: No e-mail, org/account/device ids. Conversation, session and block ids are aliased or synthetic. Cursors are epoch-ms values from the capture.
changes_vs_v1: Event.11 is NOT a turn counter. It is a value bound to the conversation (A 1 then 2 when reopened, B 4 then 5, C 2 throughout). Meaning unknown.
Window order inside Limits is NOT stable (confirmed): 7d first in one real frame, 5h first in two. v1 hex was a reconstruction and is replaced by the real frames.

'Synthetic timestamp cursor' was wrong. The cursor on opening an idle conversation is the cursor of the snapshot event the server sends on open. The client then reopens streams with the cursor of the last event it received.
Answered open questions: gzip frames are conversation snapshots without limits; limits do not arrive when an idle conversation is opened; the event after limits is a snapshot (state back to 1).
Added: end-of-turn signal for the cache timer, tests for window expiry, persistence and the capture option (status planned).

environment.extension: claude-counter, hey-naf fork v2.0.2 (Manifest V3). Content scripts: src/injected/bridge.js (world MAIN, document_start) and src/content/{constants,bridge-client,tokens,ui,main}.js plus the vendored o200k_base tokenizer. Permission: storage only. Matches https://claude.ai/*.
environment.account_A: Works. Messages go via POST /api/organizations/<org>/chat_conversations/<id>/completion; the response is text/event-stream with an 'event: message_limit' event. Plan not recorded.
environment.account_B: Free plan (analytics_subscription_plan=claude_free, billing_type=none, rate_limit_tier=default_claude_ai, capabilities=[chat]). New unified chat/Cowork UI: page telemetry says sidebar='unified'; manual/auto approval selector; attach/dictate buttons below the input box; no voice mode. Bars stay at 0%. Reproduces in an incognito window and in a fresh Chrome profile with a fresh extension install, so the problem follows the account, not the browser state. Started about two weeks before 2026-10-11.

extension_callsites_from_initiator_stack.caveat: Line/column numbers come from the user's installed build and are approximate. In the repo (hey-naf 2.0.2) the fetch wrapper in src/injected/bridge.js starts at line 28.

src/injected/bridge.js.window.fetch wrapper: repo line 28. It is in the stack of every page fetch, including PerformAction and StreamTimeline, so the hook already sees these requests.
src/injected/bridge.js.generation_start detection: repo line 35: only /completion, /retry_completion and /sessions/ match. PerformAction does not match, so the cache timer is never marked pending on the new UI.

src/content/main.js.tick: repo line 460 (calls refreshUsage every second while no usage was ever applied: lastUsageSseMs and lastUsageUpdateMs start at 0)
src/content/main.js.refreshConversation: repo line 309 (the only source of token count and cache timer)

extension_callsites_from_initiator_stack.observation: On account B, GET /usage was requested 4 times within ~3 s and always returned all-null. Explained by the tick() condition above (derived from the code, not yet reproduced in a browser).

endpoints_new_ui.PerformAction: POST /claudeai-rpc/anthropic.bard.api.v1alpha.ConversationService/PerformAction. content-type application/proto; headers connect-protocol-version: 1, x-organization-uuid, anthropic-client-build/platform/sha. Binary protobuf body (~3 KB): session id (sess_...), conversation uuid, message uuid, user text, model name, list of enabled MCP tools, locale, timezone, mode 'auto', effort 'low'. Response: 200 with content-length 0. The reply arrives on StreamTimeline. This request is the start of a turn (use it for the generation_start signal).
endpoints_new_ui.StreamTimeline: POST /claudeai-rpc/anthropic.bard.api.v1alpha.ConversationService/StreamTimeline. content-type application/connect+proto; connect-accept-encoding: gzip; response header connect-content-encoding: gzip. Long-lived server stream. Opened ~2.8 s after PerformAction in the capture, but the UI also opens it earlier (call stack shows preopenTimeline) when a chat is opened.
endpoints_new_ui.ReportViewing: POST .../ConversationService/ReportViewing, application/proto, 76-byte body (two uuids), 2-byte response. Irrelevant for limits.
endpoints_new_ui.GET conversation JSON: GET /api/organizations/<org>/chat_conversations/<id>?tree=true&rendering_mode=messages&render_all_tools=true returns the conversation (chat_messages[]) as JSON. Still works in the new UI. Token count and cache timer are computed only from it. UNKNOWN: whether the page itself re-fetches it after a turn in the new UI (probably not, state arrives via the stream).
endpoints_new_ui.GET usage: GET /api/organizations/<org>/usage returns HTTP 200 with every value null (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_oauth_apps, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_cowork, extra_usage, spend ...) and limits: []. Useless for Free accounts.

stream_timeline_request.body: One Connect frame: flags 00, 4-byte big-endian length, protobuf payload.

observed_payload_lengths.0x33 (51): no cursor, no field 6 (first open of a chat)

stream_timeline_request.cursor_note: On opening an idle conversation the server first sends one snapshot event (one gzip frame); the cursor of that event is what the client reuses. After that the client always reopens with the cursor of the LAST event it received (example: a stream ending at cursor 1791743967530-0 is followed by a request with cursor=1791743967530-0). The earlier v1 idea of a 'synthetic timestamp cursor' was wrong.

connect_framing.frame: flags(1 byte) | length(4 bytes, big-endian) | payload

flags.0x01: payload compressed with gzip (magic 1f 8b 08), per connect-content-encoding: gzip
flags.0x02: end of stream; payload is JSON: {"metadata":{...}} or {"error":{...},"metadata":{...}}

connect_framing.keepalive: 00 00 00 00 04 0a 02 32 00 (payload = event with an empty field 6). About one every 20 s (105 in the whole capture).
connect_framing.close_reasons: Stream-Close-Reason 'cadence' (initial snapshot stream closes after ~5-7 s) and 'max_age' (live stream closes after ~600 s). The client then reopens with a cursor, so one reply can span several requests.
connect_framing.size_split: All plain frames seen are below ~120 bytes; all gzip frames decompress to ~3-5 KB. The exact threshold is unknown.
connect_framing.chunking: Frames are not aligned to network chunks. Parse from a byte buffer.

event_schema_inferred.caveat: Field numbers are read from the tag bytes. Meanings are inferred from values (API is v1alpha, may change). Protobuf is a tag-length-value format: the tag carries the field number and the wire type.

Event.11: varint bound to the conversation, NOT a turn counter (A 1 then 2, B 4 then 5, C 2 throughout). Meaning unknown.

one_of.1: snapshot of conversation state (usually in a gzip frame) or 'block done' { 5: { 1: block id, 2: group id 'dgrp_...', 4: 1, 9: full text, 10: { 1: 2 }, 24: 1 } }
one_of.14: session status { 1: { 1: 'sess_...' }, 2: status varint (1 or 2 observed) }

Snapshot (gzip frame, event field 1).structure: Event.1 { 1: 1 (first snapshot only), 2: Item { 1: conversation uuid, 2: title (e.g. 'Greeting', missing at first), 3: state (2 while a turn runs, 1 idle; derived), 4: {1: epoch s, 2: nanos} created, 5: same, updated, 6: {2: model}, 7: uuid (last message/turn?), 8: Any 'type.googleapis.com/anthropic.bard.api.v1alpha.SandboxFileActivity', 10: {...} } }
Snapshot (gzip frame, event field 1).note: No limits data in any snapshot. Sub-messages that failed to parse stay as hex in the decoder output and were not searched.

Limits (event field 4).13: REPEATED { 1: window key '5h' | '7d', 2: { 1: status varint, 2: { 1: resets_at epoch seconds (varint) }, 3: utilization (fixed64 little-endian double, fraction 0..1) } }. ORDER OF THE ENTRIES VARIES between frames: read as a map by key.

mapping_to_old_sse.resolved.limit.percent: NOT present in the new stream; compute round(utilization*100)

event_schema_inferred.order_of_events_per_turn: PerformAction request -> (snapshot state 2) -> text delta(s) -> block done -> limits (6-7 ms after block done, plain frame) -> snapshot (gzip, +4-5 ms, state back to 1) -> snapshot with title (e.g. +321 ms later in conversation A). Limits arrive once per assistant turn and NOT when an idle conversation is opened. The limits event is therefore the first plain signal that a turn has ended.

test_cases.title: limits frame
test_cases.expect: 5h {utilization 0.76, resets_at 1791749400}, 7d {utilization 0.25, resets_at 1791990000}, claim five_hour, overage reason overage_not_provisioned

test_cases.title: window order independence
test_cases.input: frames limits_A_7d_first (7d first) and limits_C_turn1_5h_first (5h first), both captured

test_cases.title: non-limit events
test_cases.input: text delta, block done, session status frames
test_cases.expect: ignored, no error, no UI change. Note: only text_delta_emoji has hex; the other two are rebuilt from the decoded form.

test_cases.title: end frames
test_cases.input: end_cadence, end_error_not_found, end_error_resource_exhausted (JSON payloads built from decoded form)
test_cases.expect: stream ends cleanly, no throw, no limits emitted

test_cases.title: chunking
test_cases.input: concatenate keepalive + text delta + limits + end_cadence; feed split at every byte offset and as 1-byte chunks
test_cases.expect: same single limits result every time

test_cases.title: gzip frame (optional)
test_cases.input: wrap the limits payload as a flag-01 gzip frame; also a corrupted gzip frame
test_cases.expect: same limits result; corrupted frame ignored without exception. Plain skipping of gzip frames is acceptable for the first version.

test_cases.title: old SSE path regression
test_cases.expect: 5h 0.2 / 7d 0.12 exactly as before the patch; Connect handler is not invoked for /completion and the SSE handler is not invoked for StreamTimeline

test_cases.title: no data
test_cases.input: no limits event ever received and nothing persisted
test_cases.expect: UI shows an explicit 'no data' state instead of 0% (UI commit)

test_cases.title: repeated limits events
test_cases.input: same limits event delivered after every turn, across several streams
test_cases.expect: idempotent; the last value wins; events without windows are ignored. Values may be identical between turns.

test_cases.title: page not disturbed
test_cases.expect: the page's reader gets identical bytes; no locked or consumed body; abort/cancel is not an unhandled rejection

test_cases.title: URL scoping
test_cases.input: any other fetch (usage, conversation JSON, event_logging, rum, ReportViewing)
test_cases.expect: untouched. PerformAction only emits the generation_start signal, nothing else.

test_cases.title: generation start on PerformAction
test_cases.expect: cc:generation_start is emitted once; the request itself is passed through unchanged

test_cases.title: turn end triggers conversation refresh
test_cases.expect: a turn-end signal is emitted so the content script re-reads the conversation JSON (token count and cache timer). Works with identical limits values.

test_cases.title: expired window
test_cases.input: stored usage whose resets_at is in the past for 5h but in the future for 7d
test_cases.expect: 5h shows 0% without a stale 'resets in 0s'; 7d keeps its value (windows are judged independently)

test_cases.title: persisted value after reload
test_cases.input: usage stored after a turn, then page load without any new message
test_cases.expect: stored values are shown (expired windows as 0%), not 'no data' and not a bare 0%

test_cases.title: usage polling
test_cases.input: page with no usage data ever, 10 minutes of ticks
test_cases.expect: no more than one GET /usage per hour (plus rollover refreshes), not one per second

test_cases.title: capture option
test_cases.expect: off: nothing recorded; on: frames recorded in memory and exportable; redacted export contains no conversation text or ids

answered: gzip frames are conversation snapshots (~3-5 KB), no limits in them (fixtures.txt over the full HARs).
Opening an idle conversation delivers one snapshot and NO limits; limits arrive only live after a turn.
The event after limits is a snapshot (+4-5 ms, state back to 1), a later one carries the title.
Event.11 is not a turn counter.
